actual_GPU_trace.initial_off_trace: Target body completed and persisted results; profiling shutdown hung. Only dedicated target/CLI stopped after image/start checks. No off report exported. Fresh bounded on trace succeeded; no performance data were repeated.

tests.harness: Pytest passed with exit0; its wrapper then failed to decode cp932 log as UTF8. Preserved exact log/record, decoded separately without rerunning tests.

accepted_step_diagnostics.scope: Untimed output/accepted-step diagnostics only; no performance confirmation or new real-data accuracy claim.

optimized_CPU_component.scope: Single frozen first-step matrix only: matrix copy, original1e-3 diagonal jitter, CPU LAPACK Cholesky and solve; one pinned CPU and one BLAS thread. CSV loading/reference checks outside timing. Not full FGO or a directly paired GPU comparison.

roadmap.implementation: Pack only actually requested unique hypotheses once. Reuse observation/Jacobian input and workspace. Fuse residual changes, whitening, nuisance columns, each existing IRLS pass, small conditional solves and likelihood into one bulk request. Preserve candidate generation order and scatter outputs to original order.
roadmap.reason: Public shipped RBPF uses64 particles but a historical profile found about21 unique likelihood hypotheses. A prior NumPy prefetch was slower; that does not measure a fused CUDA implementation. Benchmark unique counts16/32/64/128/512, varying held masks and nuisance dimensions, against current cached scalar and optimized CPU native batch.
roadmap.invariant: Do not regenerate extend/shrink moves to prefetch. Shared factorization only for identical Jacobian, row weights, prior and history; IRLS/hard holds generally change these. Preserve integer/RNG/discrete decisions and all original error guards. No numeric adoption from the FGO test alone.

roadmap.implementation: FP64 square-root QR/triangular solves in bulk, one GPU workspace retained through the window; share factors only when they are exactly the same. Keep each basin history, marginalization, integer constraints and physical rows.
roadmap.reason: Potentially larger batches and matrices than the shipped3..8-dimensional likelihood. Existing dense FGO crossover is only a starting point, not a threshold for GTSAM or per-basin QR.
roadmap.invariant: Do not replace an ill-conditioned square-root QR model with normal equations merely to use Cholesky. Keep hard constraints, gauges, covariance/evidence and existing tolerances.

roadmap.scope: Existing wide-window FGO residency and sparse structure
roadmap.implementation: Measure packing pseudorange epoch blocks and moving applicable factor assembly/trial operations alongside the solver, retaining exact per-entry accumulation order. Cache capacity within the solve/window and avoid dense host/device round trips where the model permits.
roadmap.reason: Basic FGO copies a full dense GPU H to host then back for the GPU solve. VD assembles factors on host and uploads H for each solve. One800-state matrix is5,120,000 bytes. Compare optimized CPU and sparse/banded methods before claiming GPU superiority.
roadmap.invariant: Do not change default solver selection, factors, priors, damping, iteration/line-search rules or covariance output merely for speed.

roadmap.implementation: Use existing GPU LAMBDA only when multiple genuinely independent searches are available at the same decision boundary. Keep singleton/unsupported/error CPU fallbacks.
roadmap.reason: Historical shipped batch-one CUDA LAMBDA is slower; multiple particles sharing one search are not independent GPU work.
roadmap.invariant: No speculative future epochs, candidate dropping, fewer search nodes or changed retry/acceptance ordering. Exact rational/integer interval normalizers remain exact; FP64 approximations cannot replace their proof boundaries.

baseline: Existing native scalar host Cholesky vs existing cuSOLVER request; assembly/allocation/transfers/all actual iterations/host return included. This is not a comparison against an integrated optimized CPU FGO backend.
target: Public frozen experiments/rbpf_fgo runtime plus current installed native FGO. Location of any newer accuracy-winning runtime was requested; none supplied during this run.
scope_limits: Basic cases all return their initial state after one rejected line-search iteration and are excluded from useful optimization speedup claims. Preserve all original measurements without altering the fixture or repeating timing.

VD cases complete5 iterations and change position, reduce the native first-step objective, and improve synthetic position RMSE. Final ECEF position bits match CPU/GPU in these fixtures, but velocity/clock state bits differ by up to8.526512829121202e-14. This is not whole-RBPF exactness or real-data accuracy validation.

Fixed stationary12-satellite synthetic geometry with one outlier, one seed.15 samples per mode/condition; p95/p99 are descriptive small-sample quantiles, not deadline guarantees. Own last allowed CPU, normal priority, nonexclusive host/GPU.

on/auto retain silent CPU fallbacks. A separate bounded trace confirms6 Dpotrf/Dpotrs calls and GPU kernels for the large basic/VD requests; every timed sample is not separately instrumented. Profile times are not used as speedup measurements.

The LAPACK probe solves only captured first-step matrices and is not an end-to-end optimized CPU alternative or paired GPU comparison. It uses the original lower triangle and unchanged1e-3 jitter. Input asymmetry about4e-14..6e-14 is retained, not averaged.

No GTSAM/cssrlib installed in the current Python environment. No private source modification, scientific queue restart, new PPC trajectory/accuracy evaluation or new CUDA sanitizer run. Existing frozen runtime and D223/D224 maintained.
